issue.title: GC-policy and Statistics tests inherit diagnostic environment flags
issue.description: Proposing bead: sase-1n6.5.1.5.2.1.2 note 12 (also sase-1nn.3/.4/.6 and sase-1no.2). Scope three nodes: tests/ace/tui/util/test_gc_policy.py::test_freeze_happens_once (3 collections vs 2), ::test_census_off_by_default (emits a census), tests/ace/tui/test_statistics_perf.py::test_populated_perf_renderable_covers_every_panel (expects SASE_TUI_PERF off). Root cause: default-behavior tests consume inherited diagnostic flags without pinning them. Make fixtures explicitly establish the intended defaults while retaining opt-in tests; do not disable production diagnostics. Verify under both enabled and unset caller environments and run sase tool run check. Evidence includes complete failing and passing logs and SHA. Existing import budget task sase-1ic is a separate failure. Searches across ci/flake/all tasks, last-week sweep and active-epic inspection found no semantic owner for this environment-isolation gap.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic environment contrast on unchanged clean HEAD: setting SASE_TUI_GC_CENSUS=1 and SASE_TUI_PERF=1 fails all three nodes; unsetting both passes all three. Archived independent check 63ce16272c90ed2e5dca334ffbf86a98 has the identical assertions.

issue.creation_reason: Triaged the local-baseline proposal from sase-1n6.5.1.5.2.1.2 note 12 and reproduced its environment dependency. These unisolated test assumptions make unrelated agent checks fail.

payload.entry: Same ambient-diagnostics defect as sase-1np, resolved by 43314db7ad from sase-1nn.8.1.
